text: Removed the host.docker.internal extra_hosts mapping from plugin-runner in docker-compose.yml (July 2026). It is not needed: async plugin/coder callbacks reach the app via the Compose service name (http://app:3000/chat), not via the host gateway. The mapping landed on plugin-runner by accident — commit abb8b30 claimed to move it from the database service to the app service but actually moved it from app to plugin-runner. Do not re-add it to plugin-runner: plugin scripts run arbitrary code and the mapping gives them a route to services on the Docker host. If the app ever needs to reach a host-local LLM endpoint (custom baseUrl), add the mapping to the app service instead.

Baileys (@whiskeysockets/baileys) is pinned to an EXACT version in package.json, deliberately, with no caret or tilde. Do not 'tidy' it back to a range. Two reasons: upstream's 7.x prerelease tag naming is inconsistent (rc.9 vs rc14), so caret ranges over those prereleases resolve in surprising ways; and RC-to-RC releases have shipped real breaking changes (getPrivacyTokens renamed to issuePrivacyTokens, encryptMediaRetryRequest becoming synchronous). Because the library links a session to the owner's personal WhatsApp account, upgrades should be deliberate rather than automatic. package.json cannot hold a comment, which is why this is recorded here.

Related stance from the owner, decided during the rc.9 -> rc14 upgrade: if a Baileys upgrade invalidates the linked session in data/whatsapp, rescanning the QR code is the accepted fallback. Do not build session backup, migration, or auth-state-versioning plumbing for this; it is not worth the code. Baileys' useMultiFileAuthState on-disk format has been stable so far, but it is not a guarantee we defend in code.
